summary: A contents search in the window lists up to Results shown files instead of stopping at about a fifth of that for a common word: content_search asks the engine for one line a file and one file more than fits (`limit + 1`, `per_file: 1`), where it asked for four times the limit in lines at up to twenty a file. The `+` after the item count is no longer guessed from the row count. Engine::search drops the hits that aren't shown (hidden files while they are off, folders that are gone) before it cuts to the limit, and says whether a showable hit was left over (new `cut_to_limit`, `SearchResponse.truncated`). Engine::grep_cancellable says whether it ended with matches left out or files unsearched (`GrepResponse.more`). SearchStats carries `truncated` in place of the unread `total_matched`, and the status bar reads it. A marked count has a tooltip, and one row of several reads "1+ items". The content search time limit is one deadline for the whole search (`root_budget_ms`): a search location gets what the ones before it left, none is searched once the time is up, and page-full versus out-of-time is decided from the data (`page_end`), so a full page no longer reads as "stopped". A stopped search that found nothing says "Nothing Found Before the Time Limit" (new pure `empty_search_message`). Added in review: for a folder with a space in its path, which is searched together with everything around it, the engine reads a page of four times its limit, so the smaller request doesn't crowd the folder's files out.
changelog: A content search for a common word listed far fewer files than **Results shown** allows, about 100 of 500, with no sign that more matched, because it counted every matching line toward the limit. It now lists up to that many files. The `+` after the item count is no longer a guess from the length of the list: a search that finds just as many items as the limit has none, and a search whose best matches include hidden files that aren't shown no longer comes up short without one. Rest the mouse on a count with a `+` to read what to do about it. The content search time limit now covers the whole search instead of each search location in turn, so searching three locations no longer takes up to three times the limit, in the window and for `fff search`. A content search that reaches the time limit with nothing found says "Nothing Found Before the Time Limit" instead of "No Results".
behaviour_changes: A contents search in the window lists up to Results shown files. Before, it ended once 4 x limit matching lines were found at up to 20 a file, so a common word gave about limit/5 files: 100 of 500. Each row still shows the file's first matching line. Seen in review on the old code: 12 rows of 30 at a limit of 60.

The `+` after the item count comes from the search itself. Name search: shown when an item that could be shown was left out. Contents search: shown when a file was left out. A search with exactly as many results as the limit has no `+` (it had a false one). Seen in review: 5 files at a limit of 5 read "5 items" with no tooltip, at a limit of 4 "4+ items".

A name search no longer comes up short of the limit when hidden files (while hidden files are off) or folders that are gone ranked inside it: the places go to the next items. `fff find` gets the same (up to `limit` rows where it could get fewer).
A marked single row reads "1+ items".

Resting the mouse on a marked count shows "More items match. Narrow the search, or raise Results shown in Settings › Search engine.", or under a filter "More items match than the filter was given. Narrow the search." Two lines, 340 pt wide. None under a selection's "N of M selected".

The content search time limit covers the whole search across search locations, in the window and for `fff search`. Locations not reached when time is up are not searched, and the search counts as stopped. Measured in review with a scratch test (three locations of 110 files of 1.4 MB, a fuzzy search for a word that is in none): limit 1 s ended at 1.02 s, stopped, 129 of 330 files searched; limit 2 s at 2.03 s, stopped, 251 files; no limit 2.85 s, all 330, not stopped. Before, each location had the whole limit to itself.
"stopped at the time limit" is no longer shown for a search that ended at its result limit in a later location after the time had passed, and is shown when time ran out between locations.

A contents search the time limit ended with nothing found shows "Nothing Found Before the Time Limit" with "The search stopped before it had looked inside every file. Search a smaller folder, or raise the time limit in Settings › Search engine." instead of "No Results". While it runs again it says "Searching…", and "Indexing…" still comes first. With rows that a filter hides it still says "No Results".
While a search runs again the mark belongs to the results on screen, not to the limit of the search in flight. Turning a filter on used to drop the `+` at once; it now stays until the new answer.

Review fix. A contents search in a folder with a space in its path ("Tax Returns", "Application Support"): the engine reads a page of four times its limit for such a folder and still returns at most the limit. The folder is searched with everything around it, newer files first, and hits outside it are dropped afterwards. With the window's smaller request and no larger page, 50 matching files in such a folder behind 600 newer matching files elsewhere listed as "0+ items" over "No Results", where the request the window used to make found all 50; they are all listed now. `fff search --scope` in such a folder gets the larger page too, so it can return more of the folder's lines than before.

API: new `SearchResponse.truncated`, `GrepResponse.more`; `SearchStats.total_matched` replaced by `truncated`; `Finder::search_limit` gone; `GrepRequest.limit` documented as counting matching lines. The server's JSON is unchanged.

Manual: new row in the file-area messages table; the status bar's `+` bullet; the Ranking and limits paragraph (a contents search counts files, hidden files that aren't shown don't count, the `+`); the Content search time limit row (one limit for the whole search, the new message).
left_out: "Show more" link, per-search more_results state, "First N items" wording, ", still indexing" suffix: dropped by the verifier.
CHANGELOG.md: the guide forbids it; the entry is in the commit message.

Name search's fetch window: `truncated` only sees the up to max(4 x limit, 2000) candidates fff-search returns per location, so a search whose real matches reach past that window can still show fewer than the limit with no `+`. As before, and in verifier.risks.

A folder with a space in its path can still be crowded out, when more than four times the limit newer files elsewhere in the search location have the word. It then reads "0+ items" (or a few, with the `+`) over "No Results". Before this change it read "0 items" over "No Results". The `+` there can also be spurious: the page filled, and the folder's files may all have been found. The real fix is scoped-search-special-folder-names.

At the largest Results shown (5000) the tooltip still says to raise it. I left it: it needs the settings dialog's list of choices shared with the status bar, for a case that takes more than 5,000 matches.

No automated test of the deadline's wiring in the root loop (the budget handed on, `stopped = true; break` once time is up, `!aborted`, and `page_end` being given the page rather than the limit): each needs at least a second of real time. The two pure helpers are tested, and the loop was measured by hand (behaviour_changes).

No test of the call-site condition `stopped && self.results.is_empty()` in render_content; the pure function gets the combined flag. I looked at it with a throwaway flag that forced `stopped` (picture -review-stopped-nothing-forced.png): nothing found gives the new message, one file found gives the row with "stopped at the time limit" in the status bar.
Later search locations still get a page of the full limit rather than what is left of it. Not needed for correctness.
No picture of the filtered form ("5,000 of 5,000+ items pass the filter"): it needs over 5,000 matches; the UI test asserts the text and the tooltip.
cargo clippy --features term not run: src/term is untouched and calls nothing that changed (grepped src/term, src/macos.rs, src/win.rs, examples).
Not compiled for macOS or Windows. No cfg'd code is touched.
tests: tests/controls.rs: a_filtered_search_is_marked_when_more_match_than_the_filter_was_given (skips when nu is not installed; 5,010 files and a real nu run)
review_fixes: A regression for folders with a space in their path, fixed in the engine. Such a folder gets no glob, so fff-search searches the whole search location, newer files first, and the engine drops the hits outside the folder after the page is cut. The window's old request (4 x limit lines) hid that for most words. With the new request of limit + 1 files the page was full after 501 matching files anywhere. Scratch test, 50 matching files in "my folder" and 600 newer ones elsewhere, Results shown 500: the implementer's commit returned 0 hits with `more` set, where the old request (2,000 lines, 20 a file) returned all 50. Engine::grep_cancellable now gives fff-search a page of four times `limit` when the scope is inside the root and no glob is made for it (`scope_rel.is_some() && scope_glob.is_none()`, the condition search_root already uses for its larger fetch), judges the page's end against that page, and still returns at most `limit` hits. New engine test a_folder_with_a_space_in_its_name_isnt_crowded_out_of_a_content_search.

finder::tests::a_content_search_that_lists_fewer_files_than_match_says_so asserted `truncated || rows.len() == 3`, which the larger page would have made pass without testing anything. It now asks for a limit of two, where the page does fill outside the folder, and expects `truncated`; then a limit of ten, and expects all three files and no mark.

Manual, Content search time limit row: the new sentence about the whole search stood between "stops and shows what it found so far" and "The status bar then says", so "then" pointed at the wrong sentence. Moved it after.
src/finder/bars.rs imports Tooltip like the files around it instead of spelling out the path at the call.

Commit message: a paragraph on the folder with a space. The Changelog paragraph said the `+` is there "exactly when a search left items out", which the fetch window and the folder with a space make untrue; it now says the `+` is no longer a guess from the length of the list. "reaches the limit" in its last sentence is "reaches the time limit".

Checked. check.sh on the trunk commit 40f8e86: CHECK OK, 522 passed in 16 test binaries, 3/3 known root-only failures (513 on the same content one trunk commit earlier).

Tests fail without the change. Reverse-applying the src and crates diff and running the three UI tests on the old code: a_contents_search_lists_every_file_up_to_the_result_limit fails with 12 rows of 30; the other two fail at the missing tooltip (their status texts, "3+ items" and "5,000 of 5,000+ items pass the filter", are ones the old guess also gave). The unit tests name new functions and fields, so for them and for the rest I took one behaviour out at a time on the final code: the implementer's 16 one-line mutations (old page size, row-count guess, each `more` term, cut before filter, the page_end rule, `.max(1)`, tooltip, filtered text, "1+ items", selection gating, the stopped arm, both truncation terms in content_search) and four of mine (no larger page for a folder with a space, seen from the engine and from the window; the window asking for `limit` instead of `limit + 1`; the engine's `truncated` always false). Each made a new test fail. Two more passed: `limit` for `limit + 1` against the unit tests alone (the UI test is what pins it), and page_end given the limit instead of the page (it only differs when the time runs out).

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt a user, and what the code says.
(1) A search stops listing a file it used to find. In a folder with a space in its path it did: see review_fixes. Otherwise a contents search reads at least as far as before (limit + 1 files against 4 x limit lines at up to 20 a file, and a list cut at the limit either way), and a name search only gains the places hidden files and missing folders took. With several search locations a later one can now go unsearched when the earlier ones use up the time. That is the brief's point 3, the manual says so, and the search then says it stopped.
(2) The count says the wrong thing. Name search: `cut_to_limit` is exact for the candidates it is given (unit test with hidden files ranked first, and a scratch run through Engine::search in a git repository, where dotfiles are indexed). Contents search: the page is limit + 1 files, so exactly `limit` matching files can't fill it; with several locations the break at the limit only happens with limit + 1 hits in hand. Stats and rows are replaced together, so the mark is always about the rows on screen. What is left is in left_out: the fetch window, and the folder with a space.
(3) "stopped at the time limit" or the new message for a search the time didn't end, or none for one it did. `stopped` is set in two places: page_end's Stopped (files left, page not full, the root's time used up, and not our abort flag), and the deadline passing before a root is searched. A full page is never Stopped. fff-search starts its clock after the engine's `root_started`, so whenever fff-search stops for time the engine sees the time used up. With no limit, root_budget_ms gives 0, which is no limit to fff-search, and out_of_time is false. The hand measurement is in behaviour_changes.

For later briefs.
- scoped-search-special-folder-names: the grep loop has `scope_rel`, `scope_glob` and `page_limit` now. The larger page is only there because a folder with a space gets no glob; once you push a glob for every scope, delete that arm (as your plan does for the same condition in search_root) and give page_end `limit` again. Two tests pin today's behaviour and will need new expectations: engine::tests::a_folder_with_a_space_in_its_name_isnt_crowded_out_of_a_content_search (after your change a limit of 2 should give 2 hits and `more`) and finder::tests::a_content_search_that_lists_fewer_files_than_match_says_so. The loop also has `root_budget_ms`, `root_started` and `page_end`: use root_budget_ms(settings.time_limit_secs, started.elapsed()) for your retry's remaining time, and classify the pass you keep. Until you land, picture -review-folder-with-space-crowded.png shows what is left: "0+ items" over "No Results".
- empty-state-messages: the search messages come from `empty_search_message(indexed, partial, looking, stopped)` in src/finder/mod.rs, with a unit test; `capped` is `search_stats.truncated`. A truncated search with nothing listed still says "No Results" (see above); with `capped` among your inputs you can say something truer.
- preview-jump-to-match (lane-e, in progress while this landed): content_search asks `limit + 1`, `per_file: 1`, counts `truncated`, and breaks before the row that doesn't fit. Its three tests in mod.rs destructure a pair, so a third return value touches them. One line a file is enough for the jump. Raising per_file would make the engine's limit count lines again and bring the old shortfall back.
- content-match-highlight, regex-content-search: same request. The hit's `ranges` are there for the first line of each file.
- sorted-search-results: `into_hit` is no longer called "after truncation". `cut_to_limit` calls it for each hit in rank order until limit + 1 can be shown, so a stat you add there runs for up to limit + 1 hits plus the ones it drops. Sort before `cut_to_limit`.
- result-tie-break, query-history-boost, typo-fallback-near-miss, folder-filter-any-kind, multi-word-highlights, adhoc-index-feedback: Engine::search ends in `cut_to_limit(raw, limit, &needle, req.show_hidden)`, and its response literal has `truncated`. `Finder::search_limit` and `SearchStats.total_matched` are gone; `SearchResponse.total_matched` is still filled and now read by nothing.
- live-search-results, search-start-no-flash: the status bar's `+` follows `search_stats`, which is None from a new search's first letter until its answer and otherwise belongs to the rows on screen.
- search-settings-without-effect: the deadline check sits right after `root.picker.read()` in the grep loop, so time spent waiting for a lock counts against the limit. Keep it after any lock you add.
- search-settings-hints-steppers: the tooltip in src/finder/bars.rs and two places in the manual name "Results shown" and "Settings › Search engine". If a label changes, they follow.

Found, not fixed.
- A truncated contents search with nothing listed says "No Results" (folder with a space, above).
- fff-search's literal fallback gives a folder-scoped contents search that found nothing a second full time budget for that location, so one search can run to nearly twice the limit (the implementer found it; scoped-search-special-folder-names covers it).
- Files over 10 MB are never searched whatever "Content search skips files over" says (the implementer found it; search-settings-without-effect covers it).
- examples/screenshot.rs builds its engine with default search settings, so SHOT_SETTINGS can't change the time limit (the implementer's finding, not checked by me).
- In a window about 1000 pt wide with the sidebar showing, the toolbar's title is cut down to a single "." (picture -review-stopped-nothing-forced.png). The toolbar is untouched by this change; I didn't look into it.
